doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Pay on tours and doing taxes
summary: Weekly or per-show pay on tours and the tax complications.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. And I just thought wow, less than 24 hours ago I was playing for 124,000 people that thought we were okay.
Do those gigs, the Chaka Kahn and those things, were you usually paid sort of a salary or were you paid by the gig?

It varied but normally it was like a per week pay. And I guess it all depended. Sometimes it was per show or other times it was like a week’s salary. Like if you’re out there touring, let’s say you’re going to be gone six weeks or something like that, if it was a week’s salary it was pro rated of course, depending on how many gigs you actually did. They’d break it down into a day rate and then that would be reflected in your check.
I’ll bet doing taxes during those years was a bit, of a chore.

Yeah. I didn’t attempt it. So I paid the money. Because I’d end up with 1099s and I’d end up with all this different stuff coming in from all these different places. So I had to file all these different schedules, and self-employment tax and this and that. Yeah it got a little complicated.
